summary: Defines textual conventions for MIB modules that keep performance history in 15 minute intervals. It replaces RFC 2493, with changes noted in the module's revision clause. It is a draft standard.

eli5.summary: Some network statistics are saved in 15 minute chunks. This memo defines the shared way to name those chunks.

questions: what are 15 minute performance history textual conventions
how many 15 minute intervals can a mib keep
what changed from rfc 2493 to rfc 3593
subtitle: Shared data types for MIB modules that keep statistics in 15 minute buckets.

tldr.problem: Telecommunications equipment often keeps performance history in fifteen minute intervals, and every MIB module for such equipment would otherwise need its own definitions for the counters involved.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines three textual conventions, PerfCurrentCount, PerfIntervalCount and PerfTotalCount, and describes how the current interval rolls into a history of up to n intervals, along with notes on the related timing and validity objects.
tldr.outcome: MIB designers can reuse one set of 32-bit counter types. It replaces RFC 2493 with no technical changes.

today: RFC 3593 is a Draft Standard that obsoletes RFC 2493; its REVISION clause says only contact information and references changed. No later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why 15 Minute Textual Conventions
sections.content:
A manager that wants performance history from managed equipment can follow two strategies. In one, the agent counts events continuously and the manager reads the counter and works out the history itself. In the other, the agent allocates events to buckets, each covering an interval of time. Telecommunications equipment often uses the second approach, commonly with fifteen minute intervals.

The memo does not compare these strategies; MIB designers should weigh polling policy, management traffic, agent simplicity and data currentness. It only provides definitions for MIB modules that want fifteen minute history.

A textual convention (defined in RFC 2579) is a new type with a different name, similar syntax and more precise semantics than an SMI type, for the convenience of humans reading the MIB. The conventions here are based on 32 bit counts; high capacity counts are covered elsewhere.
sections.eli5: A machine can either keep one running tally or fill a new page every 15 minutes. This memo is for the second way, and it gives the pages standard labels.

sections.title: The Three Counter Types
sections.content:
The module PerfHist-TC-MIB defines three conventions, each with syntax Gauge32.

  • PerfCurrentCount: a counter for the current 15 minute interval. It starts at zero, rises as events occur, and at the end of the interval its value is stored in the first history interval and it restarts at zero.
  • PerfIntervalCount: a counter for a previous 15 minute interval.
  • PerfTotalCount: an aggregate over the previous valid 15 minute intervals. Intervals with no valid data are not counted.

Use of the conventions assumes the agent supports 15 minute history counters and can keep a history of n intervals, where n is set by the specific MIB module and satisfies 0 < n <= 96. The agent may optionally support aggregating the history, and keeps separate tables for the current interval, the history intervals and the total.
sections.eli5: There is a counter for right now, counters for earlier chunks, and one big total of the earlier chunks.

sections.title: How Intervals Roll Over
sections.content:
With IntervalCount(1) the most recent and IntervalCount(n) the least recent interval, the end of each 15 minute interval does this: the value of IntervalCount(n) is discarded, each IntervalCount(i) takes the value of IntervalCount(i-1) for n >= i > 1, IntervalCount(1) takes the value of CurrentCount, and the TotalCount, if supported, is adjusted.

The text also assumes three objects, written with the placeholder prefix xyz. xyzTimeElapsed is the seconds since the current period began, with range 0 to 899. xyzValidIntervals is the number of previous intervals for which data was collected, up to n. xyzInvalidIntervals is the number of intervals in the range from 0 to xyzValidIntervals for which no data is available, typically zero.

The overall constraint on n is 1 <= n <= 96, and any further constraint must be given in the DESCRIPTION clause of the MIB module that uses these types.
sections.eli5: Every 15 minutes the pages shift down by one: the oldest page is thrown away and the page for right now becomes the newest saved page.

sections.title: Missing Data, Proxies and Clock Changes
sections.content:
If an agent has no valid data for an interval, the matching object instance is not available. A retrieval request must return an error showing the instance does not exist, for example noSuchName for SNMPv1 and noSuchInstance for an SNMPv2 GET.

A proxy is an application that receives SNMP messages and replies for the devices where the real implementation lives, such as DS3/E3 interfaces. It may be out of contact with those devices, and so miss data and have some intervals unavailable.

The note on xyzTimeElapsed covers clock adjustments. If a time-of-day clock adjustment would push the current interval past its maximum, the agent returns the maximum value. If the agent ends intervals at 15 minute time-of-day boundaries, following the ANSI procedure, and the clock is corrected in small steps (the RFC gives 10 seconds as an example), no interval needs to be marked invalid.
sections.eli5: If a page is missing because the machine was not watching, it says so honestly instead of making up a number. A clock being nudged a little does not spoil the pages.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo only defines textual conventions for use in other MIB modules. It states that security issues for those MIB modules are addressed in the memos that define them, so this document adds no security text of its own.
sections.eli5: This memo only makes labels. Any safety rules belong to the documents that use the labels.

items.title: PerfCurrentCount
items.text: Counts events in the current interval, then restarts at zero.

items.title: PerfIntervalCount
items.text: Holds the count for one previous interval.
